cycles.en_text_before_rewrite:
# Humans Took Part in AI Phone Calls: Meta’s Strange Behind-the-Scenes Story

Was the person on the other end of the call an AI or a human? This time, at least in some cases, it was a human.

Meta was testing a phone-calling feature with Muse, its AI for personal use. But some of those calls were not handled by AI. They were handled by trained human contract workers.

The system was given the name “human concierge.” Its job was to make calls through Muse, talk with the person on the other end, and finish the task. You think AI is making the call, but behind the scenes, a human staff member appears. It is almost like a person coming out after taking off a robot costume.

Of course, we need to look at this carefully. Humans were not handling every call. It involved only some calls, and it was a test, not a finished version of a public service.

Humans making the calls is not in itself a bad thing. If the matter is complicated, things may go more smoothly if a human handles it. The problem was that the test began without properly telling the person on the other end about this fact.

The vice president of a Meta division admitted that starting a test in which contract workers made calls without proper disclosure was a “mistake.” Meta then temporarily rolled back the human concierge feature.

What we must not get wrong here is that Meta did not stop the phone service as a whole. What was rolled back was this feature in which humans made the calls.

Meta says it will continue working to improve the service with the businesses it calls, and will make it widely available only when it is ready and can explain it properly.

The interesting thing this time is that this was not a story about AI taking people's jobs. Humans were taking AI's place. But the humans who ended up in the main role had not been told. That was the problem.

Future services need more than an AI-like performance. Whether the one on the other end of the phone is an AI or a human. That is what must first be clearly explained. Meta forgot to give that explanation and, for now, brought the curtain down on the stage.

## In one line
Meta’s AI phone test used undisclosed human callers, so the company temporarily rolled back the feature.

Humans making the calls is not in itself a bad thing. If the matter is complicated, things may go more smoothly if a human handles it. The problem was that the test began without properly telling the person on the other end about this fact.

What we must not get wrong here is that Meta did not stop the phone service as a whole. What was rolled back was this feature in which humans made the calls.

開示しなかった理由を「忘れた」とし、意図や原因まで付け加えている。Ledgerは適切な開示がなかったことをミスと認めたとしているが、忘れたとは述べていない。
model_claims: Meta forgot to give that explanation and, for now, brought the curtain down on the stage.

union_candidates.claim_text: Meta’s AI phone test used undisclosed human callers, so the company temporarily rolled back the feature.
issues: 人間の電話担当者と機能の一時ロールバックは支えられますが、「so」が開示不足をロールバックの原因として結び付けています。Ledgerはその因果関係を明示していません。
「so」により、開示されていない人間による発信が機能のロールバックを引き起こしたという因果関係を示しているが、Ledgerはその因果を明示していない。
model_claims: Meta’s AI phone test used undisclosed human callers, so the company temporarily rolled back the feature.
